title: Seven people, mostly foreign tourists, killed in helicopter crash in Kenya
byline: A helicopter taking tourists on a safari has crashed in a remote part of northern Kenya, killing all seven people on board, including an Ecuadorian official and an American journalist.

title: Public Health Inspectors withdraw from dengue control duties island-wide
byline: The Public Health Inspectors’ (PHI) Union of Sri Lanka has decided to withdraw from all dengue control duties across the country, effective today (20).

title: Trump threatens ’tremendous economic consequences’ on any country helping Iran
byline: President Donald Trump has said the US will inflict ’’TREMENDOUS Economic Consequences’’ on any country that helps or does business with Iran.

title: Dengue deaths surpass 70 as cases top 93,000
byline: Sri Lanka’s dengue death toll has surpassed 70, rising to 71 as of today (20), while the total number of dengue cases reported so far this year has exceeded 93,000.

title: Retirement declarations of assets and liabilities introduced
byline: The Anti-Corruption Amendment Bill which was presented to Parliament yesterday provides provisions to make post retirement declaration of assets and liabilities legal. The amendment of Section 90 of the Anti-Corruption Act of 2023 allows a person to declare his or her assets and liabilities even after retirement.

title: El Niño : Heavier Maha rains, drier Yala raise food security concerns for Sri Lanka
byline: Sri Lanka is preparing for a potentially difficult agricultural cycle as changing weather patterns linked to El Niño raise concerns over food security, with heavier-than-usual rainfall expected during the coming Maha season followed by a significantly drier Yala season next year.

title: Sri Lanka Is the Only South Asian Country Its Neighbors All View Favorably, Pew Survey Finds
byline: A new Pew Research Center survey of public opinion in South Asia has turned up an unusual result: Sri Lanka is the only country in the region that India, Pakistan and Bangladesh all view more favourably than unfavourably. Those three countries rarely agree on much when it comes to each other. On Sri Lanka, they do.

title: Principal, teacher caught drunk on duty at exam center
byline: The supervisor and a coordinating officer of an Advanced Level Examiniation center in Medirigiriya who had been found to be under the influence of liqour

title: Daily Mirror story comes to limelight
byline: A story published by the Daily Mirror on August 18, 2026, under the title ‘Drug shortage puts cancer patients’ lives at stake’ came to light in Parliament today, with MP Shanakiyan Rasamanickam questioning a shortage of an injection given to cancer patients.

title: Another container scam : MP
byline: A fresh container scam has allegedly taken place where a red labelled container containing undeclared items has been released, SLPP MP D.V. Chanaka stated in Parliament yesterday.

title: ’Govt. has drawn up plans for debt repayments up to 2030’
byline: The government yesterday rejected claims by former President Ranil Wickremesinghe that Sri Lanka could face an economic crisis in 2027/28, arguing that foreign reserves should be viewed only as an external buffer and not as the sole indicator of the country’s economic progress.

title: Sri Lanka’s 2028 debt repayments not cause for alarm: Economist
byline: Sri Lanka is capable of meeting its debt repayment obligations from 2028 onwards despite the challenges ahead, provided the Government continues with economic reforms and takes measures to strengthen foreign exchange reserves, Professor J. G. Sri Ranjith of the University of Peradeniya said.

title: Excise officers raid Colombo Port City, including luxury party boat
byline: Sri Lanka Excise Department officers have conducted a series of raids at Colombo Port City, seizing large quantities of liquor allegedly being sold or transported without valid licences.

title: Strong winds, rough seas expected in several coastal areas
byline: Sea areas extending from Kankasanthurai to Chilaw via Mannar, and from Matara to Pottuvil via Hambantota, are expected to be rough at times, with strong gusty winds of up to 50–60 kmph, the Meteorological Department warned.

title: SL to spend USD 1,878 million for electrification of railway service: Deputy Minister
byline: Sri Lanka is to spend USD 1,878 million for the electrification of railway services across the island within the next three years, Deputy Minister Prasanna Gunasena told Parliament today.

title: President arrives at Parliament
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake arrived at the Parliamentary Complex and is currently inside the Chamber.

title: Court orders restraint on Kaduwela company over Hummer EV dispute
byline: The Colombo Commercial High Court issued an enjoining order restraining a foreign-controlled company from closing, transferring or alienating a factory in Kaduwela involved in converting vehicle drivers’ seats from left-hand drive to right-hand drive and modifying vehicles.

title: CAA conducts 108 raids on imported cosmetics and footwear
byline: The Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) conducted 108 special raids islandwide on August 18 and 19 targeting imported cosmetics and footwear, with 84 businesses found unable to produce proper receipts, bills or invoices to establish the source of the goods.

title: Russian missile barrage kills at least 13 people in Ukraine’s Kyiv
byline: Russian forces have launched ballistic missile attacks on Ukraine’s capital Kyiv, killing at least 13 people and wounding 33, officials said.

title: Blue Water Hotel denies involvement after dogs found dead near premises
byline: The management of The Blue Water Hotel & Spa has denied any involvement in the deaths of four dogs found outside the hotel’s boundary wall near the staff entrance.

title: US national debt passes $40tn after doubling in a decade
byline: US national debt has more than doubled in a decade to reach a milestone $40tn (£29.4tn), Treasury figures show.

title: Pakistan to host Sri Lanka for Tests and T20Is, England for ODI tri-series
byline: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) said in a press release that they will play three Twenty20 internationals against Sri Lanka followed by a 50-over tri-series with England in October. There will then be two Tests between Pakistan and Sri Lanka in November.

title: 14 Lamborghinis take new route through Sri Lanka due to strait of Hormuz closure
byline: While the closure of the Strait of Hormuz amid the ongoing Middle East conflict has disrupted global shipping and trade, Sri Lanka appears to be emerging as an alternative transit point for high-value cargo, with a recent shipment of 14 Lamborghini vehicles routed through the country.

title: New preschool guides launched under education reforms
byline: A set of new teacher and activity guides aimed at strengthening inquiry-based and activity-based learning in preschools has been launched under the Government’s new education reform programme.

title: BASL chief’s remark causes rumpus in Parliament
byline: A comment made by the Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL) President Rajiv Amarasuriya that the government has acted in a threatening manner with regard to  the proposed meeting of MPs with a BASL delegation which was fixed for today, brought about arguments between Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa and Chief Government Whip Nalinda Jayatissa in Parliament today.

title: Avoid sun exposure from 11 am to 3 pm - Health officials
byline: The Ministry of Health has warned the public that prolonged exposure to direct sunlight during the prevailing hot weather could cause serious heat-related illnesses and, in severe cases, lead to death.

title: Four bank officials further remanded over US$1 billion outflow scheme
byline: Four bank officials were ordered to be further remanded until September 3 by Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama in connection with an alleged scheme to transfer US$1 billion out of the country in collaboration with alleged major fraudster Jeffrey Mohamed, who is accused of establishing 36 fictitious companies under the guise of importing goods.

title: Rs. 300,000 fine for substandard helmets, expired baby milk
byline: Two business establishments in Colombo have been fined a total of Rs. 300,000 by the Aluthkade No. 05 Chief Magistrate’s Court for offering substandard motorcycle helmets and expired infant formula for sale.

title: Catholic Bishops’ Conference expresses concern over 22A
byline: The Catholic Bishops’ Conference of Sri Lanka has expressed concern over the proposed 22nd Amendment to the Constitution and the Judicature Amendment Bill, stressing that the independence of the Judiciary, the rule of law and the doctrine of separation of powers must be upheld and protected at all times.

title: Telangana Boy Stabbed Principal 27 Times. How His Lavish Lifestyle Busted Him
byline: The police in Telangana’s Nalgonda have cracked the sensational murder case of a 48-year-old school principal and arrested two students who allegedly planned the crime for money and lavish lifestyle.

title: Veteran singer Nanda Malini dies at 82
byline: Veteran Sri Lankan vocalist and one of the country’s most celebrated singers, Nanda Malini, has passed away at the age of 82.

title: Police officer allegedly commits suicide at temple
byline: A police officer assigned to provide security at the temple of Ven. Galagodaatte Gnanasara Thero has reportedly died after allegedly shooting himself with his service firearm.

title: Joint emergency response mechanism established at Matara prison
byline: A joint mechanism aimed at strengthening emergency response and improving prisoner welfare through regional coordination was established at the Matara Prison yesterday (19).

title: ASPI holds 21,400 despite third straight day of market weakness
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange extended its negative momentum for a third consecutive session on Thursday, 20 August 2026, with both benchmark indices closing marginally lower amid continued selling pressure across the broader market.

title: Joint operation launched to contain fire at Anawilundawa Ramsar Wetland
byline: A special joint operation has been launched to contain a sudden fire that broke out at the Anawilundawa Ramsar Wetland Sanctuary, with wildlife officials, the armed forces, the Disaster Management Centre (DMC), the Divisional Secretariat and local residents joining the efforts.

title: Keeping boys in school beyond 16 a growing challenge: PM
byline: Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya has warned that retaining children within the school system is becoming an increasing challenge, particularly among boys beyond the age of 16.

title: Man arrested after video of child assault goes viral
byline: A disturbing video showing a man allegedly assaulting a four-year-old girl and a seven-year-old boy while recording the incident has sparked outrage on social media, prompting police action.

title: Former Liberian vice-president charged in drug-trafficking probe
byline: Liberia has charged former Vice-President Jewel Howard-Taylor with drug trafficking, money laundering and a range of other offences as part of an investigation into an alleged transnational narcotics network.

title: Children need holidays to rest, PM says
byline: Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya has urged parents and teachers not to place excessive academic pressure on children during the current school holiday period, saying that children need time to rest, relax and enjoy their holidays.

title: Three-day national mourning declared for late Nanda Malani
byline: The Government has declared August 21, 22 and 23 as national days of mourning following the passing of veteran singer Dr. Nanda Malani.

title: Final rites of late Nanda Malani to be held on Saturday
byline: The final rites of the late veteran Sri Lankan singer Visharada Nanda Malani will be held on Saturday, August 22, at the Borella General Cemetery, according to Professor Sunil Ariyaratne.
